newsitem.title: INDIA: India's SEBI to fix rules for short sellers.
newsitem.headline: India's SEBI to fix rules for short sellers.

text.p: India's market regulator the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), said on Monday it would ask short sellers to report their short sales position at the end of each day.
Indian stock exchanges would also be asked to impose appropriate margins on shortsellers, SEBI chairman D.R. Mehta told a news conference.
"The shortseller must be asked to declare his position on shortsales at the end of the day," Mehta said. "Stock exchanges should impose appropriate margins on short sales."
Mehta said the decision to implement the rules had been taken in principle, but the exact details would be worked out by a panel of experts within three weeks' time.
"The decision has been taken in priciple, but the modalities would have to be worked out," Mehta said. "An expert group has been set up which will submit its report in three weeks."
